correctness.rationale: Nonzero equivariant pair-feature map kills standard pair module, leaving single irreducible (N-2,2) image. Constant Gram diagonal and Schur scalar fix d/(|X|(m-mu)); finite n2 k3 trace=9 and idempotence confirm normalization. All-r factorial moment proof classifies reference-block graph patterns and bounds probabilities O(N^{-(v-c)}), yielding Poisson(lambda=(k-1)^2/2) for fixed k. Uniform integrability follows from second moments; Poisson first centered absolute moment gives exact asymptotic. Iterated Gaussian moment limit gives 1/sqrt(pi). Finite checks neither replace these proofs nor imply joint scaling.

originality.rationale: Previously known pair-overlap spherical kernels and zero-overlap probability are explicitly excluded from originality claims. The final contribution is their independently normalized sharp Fourier endpoint norm and explicit first-absolute-moment Poisson amplification law with k-dependent limit. Full-primary comparisons locate strong partial coverage but no stated sharp endpoint norm limit; Bender-style broader probabilistic reduction is the chief residual risk.
residual_risks: Bender (1974) proves strong asymptotic enumeration of sparse contingency tables, and equivalent full Poisson laws may occur there or in later switchings literature; we do not claim novelty for the Poisson input as a standalone probability result.

The pair-overlap spherical representation is established in Filmus–Lindzey (2022); the finite endpoint norm is an absolute row-sum consequence of a correctly normalized kernel. The novelty assessment is focused on the explicit sharp growth constant and the normalization check.
A prior projection-norm interpretation from an alternate harmonic analysis notation, beyond inspected primary documents and searched records, cannot be excluded.

value.rationale: The first nonconstant irreducible Fourier projection on k-uniform set partitions is a natural representation-theoretic operator, and its sharp endpoint amplification is not given by the previously established extremal-intersection graph eigenvalues. The k-dependent Poisson first-absolute-moment coefficient (4exp(-2) for k=3) and iterated 1/sqrt(pi) limit give a distinct, structurally motivated quantitative invariant; a correct normalization matters for reproducible harmonic analysis. No claim of joint-limit rates or a paper-sized breakthrough is made.
